questions.prompt: A model computes mat 0.40, floor 0.25, sofa 0.15 and 0.20 for all other words. What happens next?
options: It always writes "mat", because it has the highest probability
It picks one word, with "mat" chosen about 4 times in 10
It writes all three words in order of probability
It asks the user which word to use
questions.explanation: The model picks from the list, and a likely word is picked more often. With 0.40, "mat" is picked about 4 times in 10, not every time.

questions.prompt: Why can a language model give a wrong answer in a confident tone?
options: It looks the answer up in an old database
It copies the answer from the question
It writes the text that plausibly follows the question, without checking a source
It picks the least likely word on purpose
questions.explanation: An answer is a likely continuation of the question. The model does not look anything up, so a plausible but wrong continuation reads as confidently as a right one.

questions.prompt: How does a language model differ from a phone keyboard that suggests the next word?
options: The model looks at the whole passage before the cursor, not one or two words
The keyboard learned from more text than the model
The model can only predict punctuation
questions.explanation: Both predict a likely next piece, but the model considers the whole passage so far. Because of this, it can continue a question with a fitting answer.
